items.title: Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard
items.author: Mark Minervini
items.sub: How a stock looks before a big move: the trend template and the volatility contraction pattern.
learn: Trend template: price above the 50, 150 and 200 day averages, the 200 day rising, at least 30% above the yearly low and within 25% of the high.
VCP: two to four pullbacks, each about half the last one, with volume drying up, then a move above the pivot.
Small fixed losses (7 to 8%) matter more than being right often.
items.caution: The results in the book are the author's own record, with winners picked as examples.

items.title: Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes
items.author: Brian Shannon
items.sub: Use a slow chart for direction and a fast chart for timing, so the charts agree before you act.
learn: The direction of a moving average matters more than whether price is above it.
The middle chart sets the stop (under the last higher low) and the target (next resistance).
When the timeframes disagree, staying in cash is a position too.
items.caution: The author gives rules and chart examples, not tested results.

items.title: The New Trading for a Living
items.author: Alexander Elder
items.sub: Trading psychology, risk control and the Triple Screen method in one book.
learn: Triple Screen: the weekly chart decides the side, the daily chart finds the dip, then you set the entry.
Each timeframe is about five times the next one (month, week, day).
The 2% rule per trade and the 6% rule per month keep one bad patch from ending your account.
items.caution: The Triple Screen has never been tested in a published study.

items.title: Encyclopedia of Candlestick Charts
items.author: Thomas N. Bulkowski
items.sub: More than 100 candle patterns, each measured on thousands of real charts. A Hindi edition is also available.
learn: Most popular patterns are weak: the hammer ranks 65 of 103, a doji works about half the time.
The strong ones are rare: three line strike, morning and evening star, three black crows.
Candles work better with context: with the bigger trend and at the end of a pullback.
items.caution: Use it as a reference to look up a pattern, not as a list of signals.

items.title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques
items.author: James Abbott
items.sub: A short beginner guide to reading candles: body, wick and the common one, two and three candle patterns.
learn: What each part of a candle tells you about buyers and sellers that day.
A pattern only counts after a trend and near support or resistance.
Wait for the next candle to confirm before acting.
items.caution: Good to learn the names. Tests on Indian and other markets find little edge from candles alone.
